A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JPEG Inspired Deep Learning by the same authors. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, tables and figures, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original JPEG-DL classification experiments, adversarial evaluations, compression measurements and visual analyses, including Tables 1–4 and the transformer results in Appendix A.5.

after.justification: V2 retains original classification and adversarial results and adds experiments on alternative methods, layer replacement, chroma subsampling, learning rates and inference cost in its appendix.

M1.justification: The principal input-layer JPEG-DL algorithm, soft quantizer and training objective remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 adds a localized architectural extension: replacing the first ResNet-18 ReLU with feature-space JPEG quantization, without color conversion and with a separate 8×8 quantization table for each output channel.

E1.justification: The same six classification datasets and CIFAR-100 adversarial scenarios remain. V2 removes the auxiliary image-compression evaluation reported in v1 Section 5 and Table 4. The new appendix experiments use retained datasets rather than introducing additional dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 6 adds evaluated quantization alternatives from Ballé et al. (2016), Shin and Song (2017), and Esser et al. (2019). Table 8 adds random-quality JPEG augmentation, Gaussian denoising, histogram equalization and Tu et al.'s learnable resizing. These substantially broaden comparison beyond standard training. The standalone hard-quantizer comparison in v1 Table 4 is removed.

E3.justification: Retained benchmark settings remain unchanged, but substantial new evaluation designs are added. These include layer replacement with learning rate 0.001, alpha 2 and b 6; three JPEG quality-factor ranges; three chroma formats; and a 0.003-versus-0.005 learning-rate comparison. Appendix A.12 adds full-versus-masked inference timing and throughput evaluation on ImageNet ResNet-18. These are additional protocols, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds analyses of activation replacement, chroma subsampling, learning-rate sensitivity and masked-quantizer approximation error and computational cost in Appendices A.7–A.9 and A.12. It removes v1's soft-versus-hard quantization/compression ablation. Existing adversarial tests, sensitivity plots, learned quantization tables and feature-map examples are retained, including those moved to A.10–A.11.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over three runs for the main CIFAR-100 and fine-grained results, and explicitly mention different random seeds for EfficientFormer-L1. V2's added accuracy tables follow the same practice. No changed run counts, new confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the matched EfficientFormer-L1 results are unchanged. V2 adds extensive results in Tables 6–11, including 72.10% Flowers accuracy for the new layer-replacement configuration and inference times of 5.46, 7.43 and 18.86 milliseconds for baseline, masked and full-space inference, respectively. These are newly reported conditions, not improvements to matched v1 runs. V1 Table 4's hard-quantizer accuracies and compression rates are removed.

T1.justification: The original quantizer definitions, objectives and derivative derivations in Equations (1)–(13) remain unchanged. Appendix A.12 newly defines a five-level reconstruction set centered on the uniform-quantizer output and argues for approximating the full distribution by restricting support to this set. This is a limited mathematical addition, without a general approximation-error theorem.

C1.justification: The central claims of jointly trained JPEG quantization, classification gains up to 20.9% and improved adversarial robustness remain. V2 narrows the contribution by removing claims about reducing input-image file sizes from the introduction and conclusion and removing data compression from the contribution list.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive interpretations connecting alternative-quantizer results and layer replacement to nonlinear expressiveness, and chroma-subsampling results to DNN reliance on color information. It also discusses learning-rate sensitivity and acknowledges the computational burden of full-space quantization while motivating masking. V1's interpretation that hard quantization preserves accuracy while enabling compression is removed; its foreground/background explanations remain.

D1.justification: The appendix substantially expands implementation information: alternative-baseline optimizer and initialization details, feature-layer quantization configuration, five-point masked-softmax computation, and inference measurement on a single NVIDIA RTX A5000. Masking is newly documented without establishing whether the retained benchmark runs changed implementation. The abstract also changes the stated code repository owner from JpegInspiredDl to AhmedHussKhalifa.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the principal positioning against prior JPEG-based learning remain essentially unchanged. Focused appendix additions discuss Ballé et al., Bengio et al., Shin and Song, Tu et al., and Yun et al.; the already-cited Esser et al. additionally becomes an evaluated comparator. These extend the local discussion of quantization alternatives and preprocessing without replacing the paper's overall research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most existing prose are retained. V2 locally rewrites the architecture description and gradient explanations, separates the classification-results discussion, removes the compression discussion and adds appendix subsections with updated cross-references. These are focused editorial and organizational changes alongside the scientific additions, rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to show the unified architecture and input layer. V2 adds six tables and Figure 13, including a large color-grouped comparison table, while removing v1 Table 4. Existing feature-map and GradCAM displays are enlarged or rearranged, notably Figure 12. V1 Tables 5–6 are retained as v2 Tables 4–5, not newly added results.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited comparison against alternative ways to make JPEG differentiable or preprocess images through Tables 6 and 8. The added sensitivity studies and explicit inference-cost measurements also make the method's benefits and practical costs more assessable. Removing the compression study sacrifices an ancillary result, but the corresponding claims are withdrawn. Although the masking justification remains limited, the stronger comparative evidence and computational transparency provide a clear overall improvement.
